verdict.rationale: Yapily documents a ready-built, white-label UI with pre-built institution selection and consent screens. It requires no frontend engineering for consent flows and handles SCA and bank redirects automatically, which covers the 'no institution UI' core. Consent tokens exist for retrieving accounts, but the evidence never shows the hosted flow's session-creation call, widget launch, or token handoff. Missing for 10: documented server-side session creation for the hosted AIS flow, widget/embed launch mechanics, explicit return of a consent token from the hosted flow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can let a user connect their bank with a drop-in hosted flow — create a session server-side, open the widget, and get back a token for the connected account — without building institution UI myself

citations.quote: Yapily Connect provides a ready-built, white-label open banking UI for AIS and PIS flows. Reduce development effort with pre-built institution selection and consent screens.
No frontend engineering required for consent and authorisation flows
Handles Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) and bank redirects automatically
Returns all accounts and balances for the end user associated with the presented consent token.
